claims.text: TaVCrW is a BCC refractory high-entropy alloy in its disordered solid state.
An MTP should replace the EAM reference for the liquid phase.
Free-energy perturbation should replace conventional thermodynamic integration.
The proposed method is applicable to TaVCrW at 0 GPa and 2000–2400 K.
A 12×12×12, 3456-atom supercell is suitable for MTP training and molecular-dynamics simulations.
The approach can be used with both GGA-PBE and LDA exchange-correlation functionals.
A high-fidelity MTP can reproduce the ab initio phase-space distribution of the multicomponent alloy with training errors below 1 meV/atom.
The MTP captures a broad variety of liquid-state atomic configurations.
Capturing a broad variety of liquid configurations reduces the variance of MTP–DFT energy differences.
Reduced MTP–DFT energy-difference variance improves reference–target phase-space overlap and enables efficient FEP sampling.
MTP-based FEP greatly reduces the integration-path mismatch associated with EAM-based thermodynamic integration.
An electronic Gibbs-energy contribution arises from a density-of-states gap at the Fermi level.
Solid-state short-range order stabilizes the alloy by approximately 2.4 meV/atom.
Electronic excitations shift the melting temperature by approximately 48–57 K.
The proposed method reduces computational-resource usage by approximately 80% relative to TOR-TILD.
The proposed method provides an approximately 20-fold speedup relative to TOR-TILD.
FEP using an MTP and TI using EAM will give free energies that differ by less than 0.5 meV/atom.
The original TOR-TILD method uses two EAM potentials and ab initio-MD-based thermodynamic integration.
Magnetic fluctuations have negligible effects at the relevant high temperatures.
The empirical GGA-PBE/LDA underbinding and overbinding trends remain approximately valid for TaVCrW, despite uncertainties for V and Cr.

contradictions.description: An 80% reduction in computational-resource usage leaves 20% of the original cost and therefore corresponds to a 5× speedup, not the claimed 20× speedup. A 20× speedup would correspond to a 95% reduction.
